title: bach.toml
description: How Bach Installer builds a Windows installer. Every setting: https://github.com/usebach/bach-installer/blob/main/docs/config.md

config_version.description: The version of the bach.toml format this file is written for. Optional; left out means the current one.

name.description: The app's name, as people see it.

executable.description: The Windows program to start, relative to [files] source. Needed for the Windows setup file; the macOS build names its own in [macos].

id.description: Identifies the install across versions. Never change it after a release.

description.description: One line: the shortcut's tooltip and the install page's subtitle.

source.description: The folder whose contents are installed.

allow_secrets.description: Patterns for files that look like secrets (.env, keys, .git, bach.toml) but are meant to ship.

files.description: The Windows files. Leave it out when the app only has a [macos] build.

online.description: Also build the online installer, which downloads the newest version when it runs. Needs [updates].

online_output.description: Where the online installer goes. Default dist/{name}-Web-Setup.exe.

style.description: The window's built-in style; bach styles shows each. Default bach. [style] changes its fonts, colours, corners and background.

compression_threads.description: How many threads compress the files. Default: as many as the memory budget allows, up to the number of processor cores. The setup file is the same whatever the number.

compression_memory.description: The memory budget for compressing, in MiB (default 1024). It limits the number of threads; one thread is always used.

license.description: A UTF-8 text file to accept first, or one per language.

desktop_shortcut.description: true: offered, ticked. false: offered, unticked. "always": done without asking. "never": not done.

start_menu_shortcut.description: true: offered, ticked. false: offered, unticked. "always": done without asking. "never": not done.

start_with_windows.description: true: offered, ticked. false: offered, unticked. "always": done without asking. "never": not done.

add_to_path.description: true: offered, ticked. false: offered, unticked. "always": done without asking. "never": not done.

shared_files.description: What a file that several [[components]] match needs. "first": it belongs to the first of them. "all": it is installed only when every one of them is ticked.

scope.description: user (default): installs for whoever runs setup, no administrator rights. machine: installs for every user into Program Files; Windows asks for administrator rights once.

style.description: Optional. Your own fonts, colours, corners and background on top of installer.style. Colours here apply to both modes; [style.light] and [style.dark] win.

font.description: A font family Windows has ("Segoe UI"), a .ttf or .otf file, or a list of files of one family.

heading_font.description: The headings' font; default the text's font, or the style's heading font.

radius.description: Corners of the card, the license box and the key field, in points.

button_radius.description: Corners of buttons, icon wells and checkboxes; 16 makes pill buttons.

background_image.description: A PNG or JPEG drawn over the background, covering the window.

background_image_opacity.description: How strongly the picture shows. Default 0.35.

background.description: The window's colour, or two colours for a gradient from top to bottom.

card.description: The card of choices, the license box and the key field. #rrggbbaa lets the background show through.

muted_text.description: Descriptions, the subtitle and the footer.

accent.description: Buttons, the progress bar and ticked boxes.

accent_text.description: Text on the accent. Default black or white, whichever reads.

border.description: The card's edges and its dividers.

error.description: The remove button and failure icons.

mark.description: The Bach mark and one-colour (SVG) logos.

panel.description: The panel of [layout] where it shows no picture. Default: a light tint of the accent.

panel_text.description: The heading and subtitle on the panel. Default: whatever reads on it (light on a picture).

error.description: The remove button and failure icons.

mark.description: The Bach mark and one-colour (SVG) logos.

panel.description: The panel of [layout] where it shows no picture. Default: a light tint of the accent.

panel_text.description: The heading and subtitle on the panel. Default: whatever reads on it (light on a picture).

panel.description: The panel of [layout] where it shows no picture. Default: a light tint of the accent.

panel_text.description: The heading and subtitle on the panel. Default: whatever reads on it (light on a picture).

layout.description: Optional. How the window is sized, arranged and animated. Without it the window is Bach Installer's classic column. Start from a preset and change any setting.

preset.description: A built-in layout to start from; bach layouts shows each. Every other setting here changes it.

width.description: The window's width in points. Default 540 (880 with a side panel, 600 with a banner).

height.description: The window's height in points. Default: as tall as the choices need.

panel.description: A panel beside the choices, or a banner across the top.

panel_size.description: The panel's width (left, right) or height (top) in points.

panel_inset.description: Space around the panel; with a radius it floats as a card.

panel_image.description: A PNG or JPEG that fills the panel.

header.description: Where the logo, heading and subtitle sit when there is a panel: with the choices, or on the panel.

content_width.description: The widest the choices and buttons get, centred in their room.

surface.description: The choices on the window, or on a card floating over it.

align.description: How the heading aligns. Default center (left with a panel).

logo.description: The logo above the heading, or beside it.

padding.description: Points: one number for every side, [top and bottom, sides], or [top, right, bottom, left]. Default [44, 32, 24, 32].

gap.description: Points between the heading and the choices. Default 28.

text_size.description: Text size in points; descriptions and the footer follow it. Default 14.

row_padding.description: Points inside each row of choices. Default 16.

rows.description: One card with dividers, each row a card of its own, or plain rows straight on the window.

columns.description: Separate rows in one or two columns.

icons.description: Icons in the rows. Default true.

dividers.description: Hairlines between joined rows. Default true.

buttons.description: Where the buttons sit; stretch shares the width.

primary.description: The main button after the others, or before them.

footer.description: The footer line (publisher and version): beside the buttons, above them, or not shown.

animation.description: How each page comes in. Default rise.

animation_speed.description: How fast: 2 is twice as fast. Default 1.

title.description: Text for every language, or a table of texts by language code.

description.description: Text for every language, or a table of texts by language code.

download.description: Optional. true downloads the component's files from the [updates] download link, or give an https link ({file}, {version}, {id} and {component} are filled in). The files are then not packed into the setup file: bach build writes them to a file of their own, Name-component-version.bachpack, to upload to that link, and the installer downloads it (checked against its SHA-256) only when the component is ticked.

build.description: With kind = "windows": the lowest Windows build number that works (10240 Windows 10, 17763 version 1809, 19041 version 2004, 22000 Windows 11).

run.description: Programs from your own files that setup runs: a runtime's installer, a driver. They run as the user, never through a shell.

name.description: What setup says it is doing: "Setting up {name}". The file name by default.

file.description: A packaged .exe, relative to the install folder.

arguments.description: The command line, passed as written.

when.description: install (default): after the files are in place, on a first install and every update. first_install: not on updates. uninstall: before the files are removed.

success_codes.description: Exit codes that mean it worked. 0 always counts.

ignore_errors.description: Go on when it fails (not with when = "uninstall", which never stops removal).

component.description: Only run when this optional component is installed.

elevated.description: Run this step with administrator rights: Windows asks once when it starts.

timeout_minutes.description: Minutes before setup ends the step and everything it started. 15 by default, 120 at most.

registry.description: Registry values setup writes for the user (HKCU\Software\...). Removed again when the app is uninstalled, and only while they still hold what setup wrote.

key.description: The key below the hive, starting with Software\, like Software\Vendor\App.

name.description: The value name. The key's default value when left out.

type.description: string (default), expand (text with %VARIABLES%) or dword (a number).

value.description: The data. {app} stands for the install folder.

view.description: Which registry view on a 64-bit Windows: 64 (default), 32 (what a 32-bit program reads, WOW6432Node under HKLM) or both.

env.description: Environment variables of the user. Removed when the app is uninstalled, if they still hold the value setup set.

name.description: Letters, digits and _, starting with the app id in capitals (Hello gives HELLO_) unless allow is true. Names Windows uses (PATH, TEMP, ...) and variables that inject code or redirect traffic (COR_PROFILER, NODE_OPTIONS, HTTPS_PROXY, ...) are refused.

value.description: The value. {app} stands for the install folder.

allow.description: Lets the name differ from the app id prefix. bach check warns about it.

context_menu.description: Entries in Explorer's right-click menu that start the app. On Windows 11 they sit under "Show more options".

on.description: Where it shows up: files, folders, background (the empty space in a folder), a file extension like ".md", or a list of them.

arguments.description: The command line after the program. "%1" (the clicked item) by default, "%V" for the background.

services.description: Windows services the app installs. Needs installer.scope = "machine". Setup creates each service, starts it, stops it while files are replaced and deletes it when the app is removed; it only ever changes a service whose program is in the install folder.

name.description: The service's name, as `sc query NAME` knows it: letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, up to 64 characters.

display_name.description: The name Services lists. The service's name by default.

file.description: The service's program, a packaged .exe relative to [files] source. The app's own program by default.

arguments.description: The command line after the program.

start.description: When it starts: with Windows (auto, the default), a little after it (delayed), when something asks (manual) or never (disabled).

account.description: Who it runs as. local_service (the default) has few rights on this computer and none on the network; local_system has full rights.

restart_on_failure.description: Let Windows start it again a minute after it stops by itself, three times. true by default.

firewall.description: Windows Firewall rules that let the app's traffic through. Needs installer.scope = "machine". Setup adds each rule and deletes it when the app is removed.

name.description: The rule's name in Windows Defender Firewall.

file.description: A packaged .exe the rule is for, relative to [files] source.

direction.description: in (the default) lets other computers connect to the app; out lets the app connect out.

protocol.description: any by default; ports need tcp or udp.

ports.description: Local ports: 8080 or "8080,9000-9010". A rule needs a file or ports.

networks.description: Where it applies: domain, private, public, or a list of them. Every network by default.

migrate.description: Older installs of this app that another installer made (Inno Setup, NSIS, MSI). A first install removes them before placing files, using the uninstall command listed under Settings > Apps.

uninstall_key.description: The name of the old install's entry under ...\CurrentVersion\Uninstall: {AppId}_is1 for Inno Setup, the product code for an MSI, the chosen name for NSIS.

arguments.description: Arguments that make the old uninstaller run quietly (/VERYSILENT /NORESTART for Inno Setup, /S for NSIS). Used when the entry has no QuietUninstallString.

elevated.description: Also remove a machine-wide old install; Windows asks for administrator rights.

updates.description: Lets the installed app update itself. Give github (owner/repo) or a feed link.

github.description: owner/repo: updates come from that repository's GitHub releases (the Bach Installer action publishes them).

feed.description: The https link of the update feed (latest.json). Not needed with github.

download_url.description: Where the setup file will be downloaded from. {file} is its name, {version} the app version.

mirrors.description: More feeds to ask when the main one can't be reached. Each is a full feed (latest.json) with its own download link. The first feed that answers decides the newest version; the others only give other places to download the same file (same version and SHA-256).

auto.description: Keep the app up to date in the background: true (offered, ticked; the default), false (offered, unticked), "always" or "never".

public_key.description: The publisher's Ed25519 public key (bach feed-key makes one). With it, the installed app accepts only feed entries signed with the private key, whichever host or mirror served them.

next_public_key.description: A second Ed25519 public key that is trusted too, to hand over to a new key (needs public_key): entries signed with either key are accepted.

max_age_days.description: How many days old a signed feed entry may be (needs public_key). The entry carries the time bach feed signed it; an older one is ignored, which stops a taken-over host from serving an old, validly signed entry for ever. 0 or left out: no limit. The feed has to be signed again (bach feed) within that time, release or not.

beta_feed.description: The https link of the beta channel's feed. An installation that chose beta versions (uninstall.exe --channel beta) asks this feed instead of feed and mirrors. The same keys and signer apply.

signer.description: The publisher a downloaded update has to be signed by (Authenticode): the common name or organisation of the signing certificate, like Example Inc., or its whole subject (CN=..., O=..., L=..., C=...), which has to match exactly. An update that is unsigned, not valid for Windows or signed by anyone else is refused. On a Mac it needs an Apple-issued Developer ID Application signature with that name; there a whole subject is CN=name, OU=team id.

access.description: Ask for an access key before installing, and encrypt the packaged files with it. The key is never written here: the build reads it from an environment variable (make keys with `bach key`).

encrypt.description: Encrypt the packaged files with the key. Default true.

key_env.description: The environment variable that holds the key while building. Default BACH_ACCESS_KEY.

get_key_url.description: Where people get a key. The key page offers a button to it.

send_key.description: Send the key as Authorization: Bearer <key> with every request to the update feed and the download, so a private server can refuse anyone without one. Default true with [updates].

signing.description: Optional. How to sign the setup files; bach build --sign (or BACH_SIGN=1) then signs them. Without it nothing is signed.

program.description: The signing program. signtool by default.

arguments.description: Its arguments. For signtool they start with the word sign. The setup file is added last; write {file} to put it elsewhere. {env:NAME} is replaced by an environment variable.

profiles.description: Optional. Other builds of the same app from this file: [profiles.NAME] holds only what differs. bach build --profile NAME builds one, bach build --all-profiles all of them.

kind.description: What the profile builds: a setup file (default) or a ZIP of the files, to unpack and run without installing.

description.description: One line about what the profile is for; bach profiles shows it.

output.description: Where this profile's file goes. {name}, {version} and {id} are filled in. A setup file ends in .exe, a ZIP in .zip.

app.description: Replaces the settings of [app] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

updates.description: Replaces the settings of [updates] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

access.description: Replaces the settings of [access] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

signing.description: Replaces the settings of [signing] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

style.description: Replaces the settings of [style] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

layout.description: Replaces the settings of [layout] it names (a table is merged key by key, an array is replaced as a whole).

arch.description: Replaces the settings of [arch] it names (a table is merged key by key).
Optional. The app's files for another processor architecture. [arch.arm64] makes bach build an ARM64 setup file next to the x64 one and list both in the update feed.

arm64.description: The ARM64 build of the app.

source.description: The folder with the ARM64 files, relative to bach.toml. It is packed instead of files.source.

exclude.description: files.exclude for this folder. The main files.exclude when left out.

runtime.description: The ARM64 bach-setup.exe to build the ARM64 setup file on, relative to bach.toml. Left out, --runtime-arm64 or BACH_RUNTIME_ARM64 names it.

macos.description: Optional. The macOS build of the app: bach build --platform macos packs it into a Setup app in a .dmg next to the Windows setup file. The name, version, texts, look, choices and updates are shared with the rest of bach.toml.

source.description: The folder with the macOS files, relative to bach.toml: usually the app bundle (Hello.app) and anything beside it.

executable.description: The program to start: an app bundle (Hello.app) or a program inside source. app.executable when left out.

exclude.description: files.exclude for this folder. The main files.exclude when left out.

executables.description: Patterns of files that must be programs, like Hello.app/Contents/MacOS/*. Needed when the folder comes from a computer that doesn't keep the executable bit (a Windows checkout, a zip).

output.description: Where the setup file goes; must end in .dmg or .zip. {name}, {version} and {id} are filled in. dist/{name}-Setup-{version}.dmg when left out.

data.description: Folders like ~/Library/Application Support/Hello that the uninstaller deletes when the user ticks 'Also delete my data'.

icon.description: A .icns file for the setup app and the uninstaller.

bundle_id.description: The setup app's bundle identifier, like com.example.hello.setup. Made from the app id when left out.

minimum_version.description: The oldest macOS the app runs on, like "12.0". Setup refuses to install on an older one.

name.description: What setup says it is doing: "Setting up {name}". The file name by default.

file.description: A packaged .exe, relative to the install folder.

arguments.description: The command line, passed as written.

when.description: install (default): after the files are in place, on a first install and every update. first_install: not on updates. uninstall: before the files are removed.

success_codes.description: Exit codes that mean it worked. 0 always counts.

ignore_errors.description: Go on when it fails (not with when = "uninstall", which never stops removal).

component.description: Only run when this optional component is installed.

elevated.description: Run this step with administrator rights: Windows asks once when it starts.

timeout_minutes.description: Minutes before setup ends the step and everything it started. 15 by default, 120 at most.

run.description: Programs setup runs for the macOS build, like [[run]] does for Windows: files with the executable permission.

signing.description: How bach build --sign signs the macOS setup app.

identity.description: A code signing identity, like 'Developer ID Application: Example (TEAMID)'. '-' signs ad hoc.

notarize.description: A notarytool keychain profile. When set, the build submits the .dmg to Apple, waits and staples the ticket.

installer_identity.description: A 'Developer ID Installer' identity that signs the .pkg bach build --pkg writes.

agents.description: Background programs of the app, run by launchd for the user who installed it: the Mac's counterpart of [[services]]. Each becomes a launch agent app.bach.agent.<app id>.<name>, loaded with the install, replaced by an update and removed with the app.

name.description: Names the agent: letters, digits and dashes.

file.description: The program, a packaged file with the executable permission. app.executable when left out (and that is a program, not a bundle).

arguments.description: Its arguments, written like a command line; nothing is expanded and no shell runs.

run_at_load.description: Start it at sign-in and when the install finishes. true when left out.

keep_alive.description: Start it again whenever it ends. false when left out.

interval.description: Run it again every this many seconds.
